Definition: from G1537 and a derivative of the neuter of G3762; to make utterly nothing of, i.e. despise:--set at nought. See also G1848.
BiblicalUsage: exoudenóō is how Scripture says to despise, to set at nought. In Mark 9:12, the text says "and be set at nought."
TheologicalSignificance: I take exoudenóō as it stands: to despise, to set at nought.
